subject: RFP response: Observable SLA framework, regional probe sampling & service-credit matrix
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@omniscience.com>

Cc: procurement@omniscience.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: OmniScience RFP - SLA measurement methodology and evidence request

Jonas,

Thanks for taking our RFP. The procurement committee has a few follow-ups specifically on SLA/SLO measurement and credits before we move to legal redlines. Could you scope the following and send any supporting evidence?

- Explicit uptime definition (what endpoints are measured, regional breakdown)
- Latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) and how you handle tail latency and multi-region sampling
- Measurement methodology: probe vs agent-based, sampling frequency, clock sync assumptions, and how you handle synthetic probe maintenance windows
- Service credit calculation and an example (30-day window) including burst attenuation and partial-region degradation handling
- Evidence bundle: single-source telemetry examples, probe configs, and any prior incident adjudication examples (anonymized)

Our deadline for answers is EOD 2028-02-17 PST. If you can share a draft earlier that would help the evaluation team.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Procurement
OmniScience, Inc.

Attachment: Omni_RFP_SLA_Questions_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

Team — forwarding OmniScience's follow-ups. Their ask is focused and they've given us a week. Can we pull together a consolidated response and a short evidence bundle?

Proposed owner split:

2) Clock sync — they specifically asked about assumptions; we should explicitly call out NTP/PTP expectations and how we normalize in multi-region windows.

I'll own the final doc and coordinate sign-off. Target draft to me by Tue EOD (2028-02-14) so we can iterate.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OmniScience RFP - SLA measurement methodology and evidence request

Jonas / Laura —

Draft answers / technical points below. I attach a concise probe sampling plan (probe_sampling_plan.yaml) with recommended frequencies and regional shard logic. Key items:

- Measurement sources: primary = Redwood synthetic probes (regional), secondary = customer-side agents (optional) for attribution. We recommend probe placement in each target region (minimum 3 probes per region across AZs) to avoid single-host bias.
- Sampling frequency: continuous probes at 1m cadence for P50/P95 tracking; 15s cadence for short-term tail analysis during incident windows (burst sampling). Aggregation windows for SLA computation: 5m windows with 30-day sliding window for monthly SLOs.
- Clock sync: assume NTP with max skew 250ms for cloud regions; for on-prem we require documented clock sync policy (NTP/PTP). We normalize timestamps at ingestion using server-reported offset and apply a correction factor for percentiles.
- Tail handling: use weighted percentiles with blackout for known maintenance windows. For partial-region degradations we compute region-weighted availability (traffic-weighted by Redwood routing estimates) and provide both per-region and global availability figures.
- Evidence format: single-line JSON telemetry per probe sample (ts, probe_id, region, rtt_ms, status). We will include a sample of 72 hours in the evidence bundle.

Attachment: probe_sampling_plan.yaml (text/yaml)

Questions for Laura: any constraints on the blackout/maintenance definition we should use in contractual language? I can add a short example calc for a 30-day month showing service-credit math.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OmniScience RFP - SLA measurement methodology and evidence request

Karthik / Jonas —

Thanks — that technical approach looks good. A few procurement/legal notes and a service credit template attached:

- Service credit baseline: propose monthly uptime target = 99.95% (global), with per-region sub-SLOs called out. Credits tiered: 99.95-99.5 => 10% credit; 99.5-99.0 => 25%; <99.0 => 50% (example matrix in attached spreadsheet). We should label this as "negotiable" in the RFP but provide a clear worked example (I will include a 30-day calc).
- Burst attenuation: apply a 1-hour burst window normalization to avoid penalizing temporary transient congestion caused by flash traffic; we should state the formula and cap (e.g., cap creditable minutes from bursts at X per month).
- Attribution: clarify that Redwood will provide both Redwood-measured and customer-provided telemetry; default adjudication uses Redwood telemetry unless customer provides authoritative agent logs for the same timestamps to dispute. Include an escalation path (CS -> Eng -> Legal) and SLA evidence request process (how they request a re-eval).
- Maintenance windows: propose standard pre-scheduled maintenance with minimum 48h notice; emergent maintenance for security patches may be excluded with post-facto notice and joint incident review.

Attachment: service_credit_matrix_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

I'm comfortable with the draft language; once Karthik confirms the probe sample example calc I'll assemble the contract-ready appendix.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Contracts & Procurement Operations
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Feb 2028 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: OmniScience RFP - SLA measurement methodology and evidence request

Marta —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is our consolidated RFP response focused on observable SLA mechanics, probe sampling, and example credit math: Redwood_OMNI_RFP_SLA_Response_20280215.pdf.

What we've included (high level):
- Precise uptime definition: endpoint-level availability for the inference API (POST /v1/generate and streaming endpoints) measured per-region and aggregated globally.
- Latency SLOs: default hosted API targets: P50=50ms, P95=220ms, P99=600ms (these are for our hosted tier; we include a section describing expectations for Dedicated & Private which notes higher variance and measurement guidance).
- Measurement methodology: primary: Redwood synthetic probes (regional), secondary: optional customer probes/agents. We include the probe_sampling_plan.yaml and a 72-hour telemetry sample (in evidence bundle) showing raw probe JSON lines and computed sliding-window percentiles.
- Clock sync & normalization: we call out NTP expected behavior and show our ingestion offset correction approach.
- Burst attenuation & partial-region handling: we provide the formula used for a 30-day window, an example calculation (worked example included), and the service credit matrix.
- Attribution & disputes: default to Redwood telemetry with a documented evidence request & adjudication flow; timeline for dispute resolution (30 days) and contact points.

Attachments included:
- Redwood_OMNI_RFP_SLA_Response_20280215.pdf (contains the narrative + worked examples)
- evidence_bundle_sha256.txt (SHA256 of tarred evidence)
- probe_sampling_plan.yaml (technical plan)
- service_credit_matrix_v2.xlsx (example credit tiers & worked 30-day calc)

Links: Evidence pack is on our internal Drive (https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/OMNI/evidence-pack-20280215). If you need a downloadable tarball or an sftp transfer for legal review, we can produce that.

Next steps: please confirm if you want us to move any of the draft numbers into contract-ready language (we flagged negotiable items in the PDF). We can also schedule a 45-minute technical walk-through with Karthik and Laura next week if the committee wants to go deeper on probe math or attribution.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
